summary: Summation No. 23 covers August 1947 (many statistics are for July or June), in the second year of the Occupation. Politically it records the creation of a Ministry of Labor on 28 August under Mitsusuke Yonekubo, the Katayama Cabinet's coal-control dispute with the Liberal Party, which scrapped the Four-party Agreement on 12 August, Prime Minister Katayama's 17 August appeal to the nation, and Councillor by-elections. A long analysis of the April 1947 elections gives vote counts, Purge screening, women candidates and campaign finance. Legal sections report the new Supreme Court and war crimes trials, including Pacific-phase tribunal testimony. Economic sections give production, labor, trade, rationing, price-control, banking and property-custody figures, with floods, coal shortfalls and first postwar foreign-trade shipments. Social sections cover epidemic disease, textbooks and media. The appendix reviews the second Occupation year (1 September 1946 to 31 August 1947), a useful overview for historians. The scan ends at printed page 336, so the Map of Japan is the last item.
highlights: A Ministry of Labor was established on 28 August (Labor Ministry Law passed 29 August), with Social Democrat Mitsusuke Yonekubo as first Minister, handling all labor matters except those of seamen.
The Liberal Party scrapped the Four-party Agreement on 12 August and declared itself in opposition; Secretary General Banboku Ono announced on 23 August a movement to overthrow the Katayama Cabinet.

Coal control caused wide political controversy: the Democrats announced a 19-point program on 4 August, opposed by the People's Cooperative and Social Democratic Parties, while the July coal quota was beaten by 10,300 metric tons.

In the April 1947 local elections, independents won 9,257 of 10,419 mayoralties, 31 of 46 governorships and 173,999 of 193,881 assembly seats; ten of 19 women candidates won House of Councillors seats.

The first Supreme Court under the new Constitution was organized with a Chief Justice and 14 associate justices; war crimes work completed 12 trials of 37 persons, with 4 acquitted and 33 sentenced to 18 months to life.

First agricultural land sales under the Land Reform law were completed: 24,325 cho (59,621 acres) bought by tenants in 12 prefectures; northern Honshu flood damage was estimated above 7,000,000,000 yen.

Foreign trade reopened: cotton fabrics went to 19 countries in July (68,138,000 linear yards) and the first postwar Davao hemp arrived from the Philippines; Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 150,684,000,000 yen on 31 August.

Mitsui Trading and Mitsubishi Trading began liquidation under the Holding Company Liquidation Commission, with loans of 200,000,000 and 120,000,000 yen for operating funds; the Reconstruction Finance Bank had lent 17,982,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 23, August 1947, table of contents and list of charts, maps and graphs, 106 items from industrial production indexes to the Map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no SCAP reorganization, new Ministry of Labor, coal-control politics, land sales, steel, trade, rationing, finance and property control.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Reports no change in the organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during August 1947.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Ministry of Labor created 28 August, Katayama's 17 August appeal, party reactions to coal control, April election analysis, Purge Appeal Board members to Supreme Court, juvenile police departments and war crimes figures.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: First land-reform sales, northern Honshu floods, coal quota beaten by 10,300 tons, steel and aluminum gains, first Davao hemp, 150,684,000,000 yen note circulation, property custody and the industrial production index chart.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Summary of public health and welfare and education developments for the month, introducing Part IV material.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed coverage of the new Ministry of Labor, coal control, parties, the Diet, the April 1947 elections, public safety statistics, the new Supreme Court and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Yonekubo's appointment as Labor Minister, coal-control disputes, Liberal break with the coalition, Communist and Democratic Party positions, and a long analysis of the April 1947 elections with vote tables.

sections.title: Administration and Political Developments
sections.summary: Ministry of Labor creation, coal control, House of Councillors by-elections in five prefectures, food release and Prime Minister Katayama's 17 August appeal.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Democratic 19-point coal plan, Liberal sponsorship of the All-Japan Farmers' Union on 3 August and break with the coalition on 12 August, Communist attacks on the Cabinet.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Joint Legislative Committee, standing committees and free debate sessions of the Diet in August.

sections.title: Analysis of the April Elections
sections.summary: Significance, laws, Purge screening, publicity, local and national results, women's participation, abstention rates and campaign financing of the April 1947 elections, with election vote charts.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Brief note on Purge Appeal Board members appointed to the Supreme Court.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Railway casualties, criminal offenses and prefectural crime rates, police juvenile departments, prison population of 78,147 in July and June fire losses of 226,738,226 yen.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Organization of the first Supreme Court under the new Constitution, 79 new suspects ordered arrested, 1,089 held in Sugamo, and tribunal testimony on Pacific-phase, diplomatic and naval planning.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Production, labor, trade, price, finance and property statistics for July and August 1947 across twelve economic sections, with charts and tables.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Tenant land sales of 24,325 cho, 269,943 cho received for taxes, reclaimed land use, northern Honshu flood damage, July fish catch and fishing vessel fuel allotments.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Falling July log output, firewood, charcoal and camphor, coal production beating quota by 10,300 tons then declining in August, stockpiles, lignite and the Imperial Oil Company's new well.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke, steel, aluminum, copper, cement, construction, shipbuilding, chemicals, machine tools, rolling stock and textile machinery output for July.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Food processing, alcohol, tobacco, pulp and paper, glass, ceramics, electrical goods, motor vehicles, rubber, leather, farm implements, watches, sewing machines and consumer goods.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: July cotton, silk, rayon, wool, hard-fiber, knitting, finishing and clothing production, mill stocks and machinery, with textile production indexes.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Motor, rail, coastal and foreign shipping, electric power generation of 3,482,000 kW water availability at 112 percent of average, consumption of 2,112,100,000 kWh in June, and gas.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Foreign communications expanded after trade reopened, telegrams, telephone service, radio licensees, postal and savings services, equipment manufacture and Ministry of Communications personnel.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor Ministry Law passed 29 August, union membership, 72 disputes involving 45,223 workers in June, Central Labor Relations Committee ruling, wage demands, labor schools and Occupation labor.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: July trade by commodity group, including cotton fabric exports of 68,138,000 yards to 19 countries and first postwar Philippine Davao hemp, plus food, machinery, chemicals and metals.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Full month's ration for the nine largest cities, potato and summer-grain collections, controls on processed fish and vegetables, producers' goods price rises and urban family expenditures.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Note circulation of 150,684,000,000 yen, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans of 17,982,000,000 yen, bank deposits, Japan Securities Exchange share offering of 945,000, closed institutions liquidation and national debt of 300,882,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Foreign nationals' property of 1,399,909,000 yen, war suspects' property of 85,377,000 yen, precious metals in custody, Hayashikaze restricted, Mitsui and Mitsubishi Trading liquidation, 147 plants inspected for reparations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, vital statistics, education, religion, arts, radio, press, films and theater reports for the month.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Communicable disease counts by prefecture, insect and rodent control, veterinary and milk inspection, medical and dental supply distribution, hospitals and vital statistics.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Secondary school reorganization, teacher workshops, adult education, O-bon festivals, monuments, information programs, radio, press comment, motion pictures, theater and music.

sections.title: Appendix: Review of the Second Occupation Year, 1 September 1946 - 31 August 1947
sections.summary: Retrospective summary of the second Occupation year covering food, inflation, democratization, labor, industry, trade, communications, finance, property control and reparations.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization under SCAP
sections.summary: Summary of GHQ, SCAP organization changes across the second Occupation year.

sections.title: Section 2. Securing of Necessities of Life
sections.summary: Food imports and the summer food crisis, land reclamation, shelter, the White Paper and stabilization program against inflation, public welfare and health.

sections.title: Section 3. Progress of Democratization
sections.summary: New Constitution, 1947 elections, Purge, courts, International Military Tribunal and Class B and C trials, agrarian reform, labor, antitrust, education, religion and media.

sections.title: Section 4. Economic Progress
sections.summary: Year's progress in coal, heavy industry, textiles, foreign trade, transport, communications, finance (Reconstruction Finance Bank 17,982,000,000 yen), property control and reparations committee set up May 1947.
